overview: Traces a fourth-quarter 1946 Japanese abaca allocation: State tentatively authorizes 685,000 pounds of fiber plus monthly tow; SCAP later confirms action pending, then requests RFC confirm grades and ship from the Philippines, with landed-price terms and SCAP export-fund payment authorized.

people.name: J. K. McCormick
people.role: Clearance official, listed with the code or initials JK

people.name: Henry
people.role: Office of International Trade clearance official

subfiles.title: State Department authorization for Japanese abaca allocation
subfiles.to: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers (SCAP), Tokyo
subfiles.about: The Department tentatively authorizes an abaca allocation for Japanese cordage production and instructs SCAP to begin negotiations with the Reconstruction Finance Corporation.
subfiles.summary: State tentatively sets a fourth-quarter 685,000-pound Japanese abaca fiber allocation plus 100 monthly tons of tow, directing SCAP to negotiate with the RFC, after interagency clearance.

subfiles.title: SCAP notice that action on the abaca allocation is pending
subfiles.to: U.S. Department of State, Washington, via the War Department
subfiles.about: SCAP acknowledges the State Department’s abaca instruction and reports that a substantive reply will follow when action has been taken.
subfiles.summary: SCAP relays that action on the September abaca allocation telegram remains pending, promising a reply soon.

subfiles.title: SCAP request for RFC confirmation and shipment of abaca
subfiles.from: General Headquarters, Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers, Tokyo
subfiles.about: SCAP asks the Reconstruction Finance Corporation to confirm abaca quantities and grades, arrange shipment from the Philippines, and accept payment from the SCAP export fund.
subfiles.summary: SCAP requests RFC confirm and ship 685,000 pounds of abaca fiber and monthly tow for Japan at a landed-price formula, authorizing payment from the SCAP export fund.

interest: Shows U.S.-run allocation of Philippine abaca fiber for Japanese cordage manufacture via SCAP and the RFC.
